confidence.rationale: The official location, current dinner, happy-hour, and general food pages were reopened. They strongly establish material baseline and extraction defects, while inaccessible brunch and wine-list PDFs and the absence of an allergen matrix prevent complete allergen or cross-contact adjudication.

confirmedFindings: The packet identifies 20 affected baseline items. Reconciliation covers all 35 baseline items: 11 artifact/accurately_unavailable, 2 variant_match/verified, 7 exact_match/verified, 6 exact_match/accurately_unavailable, 2 exact_match/mismatch, 5 missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable, and 2 artifact/not_applicable.
The current official location page confirms the 14th Street identity and four menu surfaces: dinner, brunch, full wine list, and happy hour.
The two-page dinner PDF is fully readable and contains substantially more products than Luna catalogued, confirming scope incompleteness, count drift, current-only omissions, and validation concerns.
The happy-hour PDF confirms its four snack products and the duplicate Charcuterie & Cheese presentation.
The brunch and full-wine-list PDFs remained inaccessible, so related baseline matches and current scope remain unverifiable.
The frozen catalog contains clear extraction artifacts and category corruption, including headings and wine-table fragments represented as products.

Gambas al Ajillo explicitly names shrimp through the item identity, supporting shellfish but not the frozen fish declaration. Lomo Ibérico has no restaurant-issued support for the frozen tree-nut declaration.

No restaurant-issued allergen matrix, complete ingredient list, negative allergen claims, may-contain statement, or cross-contact disclosure was found. Empty arrays therefore cannot establish allergen absence.

Narrow positive evidence remains valid where the menu explicitly names ingredients or an allergen-bearing identity, including named milk cheeses, shrimp/mussels/clams/calamari, salmon/branzino/hamachi, walnuts/almonds/pistachios, tahini, and sour cream.
The dinner instruction to inform the server about food allergies is not evidence of cross-contact, shared equipment, or may-contain status.
rejectedFindings: Reject any upstream interpretation of the dinner allergy notice as a cross-contact disclosure.
Reject treating inaccessible or incomplete menu coverage as support for negative allergen conclusions, complete allergen arrays, or complete restaurant scope.

Reject Terra's promotion of egg for Potato Tortilla and Basque Burnt Cheesecake solely from customary recipes; those are culinary assumptions, although sour cream explicitly supports milk for Potato Tortilla and cheesecake identity narrowly supports milk.
Reject Terra's egg-and-milk assignment for Flan Catalán absent explicit ingredients; the dish name alone does not establish this restaurant's formulation reliably enough for allergen data.

Reject Terra's milk assignment for Ice Cream from the item name alone; pistachio explicitly supports tree nut, but non-dairy formulations make milk non-unavoidable without further restaurant-issued evidence.
Reject over-correction that would erase explicit positive evidence merely because no complete allergen matrix exists.

additionalEvidence.summary: Confirms the 14th Street Washington, DC location, address, brunch service, and links to dinner, brunch, full-wine-list, and happy-hour menus.
Current two-page dinner menu confirms extensive omitted scope, parser artifacts, explicit positive ingredients, and only a server-notification allergy instruction.
Confirms the happy-hour products and duplicate Charcuterie & Cheese presentation.
Contains general culinary marketing but no item-level allergen matrix, ingredient database, negative claims, or cross-contact disclosure.
Officially linked current brunch source remained unretrievable, preserving the scope uncertainty.
Officially linked full-wine-list source remained unretrievable, preserving uncertainty around wine-related baseline entries.

summary: The mandated effective outcome is low_confidence. Terra correctly identified material scope, extraction, and baseline-allergen problems and correctly withheld negatives and cross-contact conclusions. Sol narrows several Terra positives that depended on customary recipes while preserving explicit restaurant-issued ingredient and unavoidable named-identity positives. The baseline requires repair, but inaccessible menu surfaces prevent complete verification.

Remove or reclassify confirmed headings, wine fragments, and other non-product artifacts.
Correct Gambas al Ajillo from fish to narrow shellfish evidence and remove unsupported tree nut from Lomo Ibérico.

Do not promote inferred egg or milk for Flan Catalán, inferred egg for Potato Tortilla or Basque Burnt Cheesecake, or inferred milk for Ice Cream without stronger restaurant-issued evidence.
Re-research the officially linked brunch and full-wine-list PDFs before attempting complete scope reconciliation.
